name: Why Vietnamese Students Are Increasingly Choosing Europe for Higher Education

description:
Shifting trends and what they mean for global education consultants

In recent years, Vietnam has emerged as one of the fastest-growing outbound student markets in the world. Traditionally, countries such as the United States, Australia, and Canada have dominated as preferred destinations. However, Europe is quietly but steadily rising in popularity among Vietnamese students seeking international education.

At Collab International, we have observed a clear uptick in demand from Vietnamese partner agencies and student clients for European universities—particularly in destinations such as Germany, France, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, Hungary, and Italy. This article explores the factors driving this shift and what education consultants should know in order to respond effectively.

For many Vietnamese families, affordability is a primary consideration. European countries, especially those in Central and Eastern Europe, offer highly competitive tuition fees when compared with Anglo-Saxon destinations. Additionally, the cost of living in cities like Prague, Budapest, and Warsaw is substantially lower than in London, Sydney, or Toronto.

Importantly, lower cost does not imply lower quality. Many European universities are ranked globally, with strong research output and a growing number of English-taught programs—particularly at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels. Countries like the Netherlands and Germany have long offered a wide selection of English-medium degrees, and now even smaller systems like Czechia and Lithuania are following suit.
